_comment: Resource policy on the SELFIE bucket. Applied with:
aws s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket <SELFIE_BUCKET> \
--policy file://deploy/iam/selfie-bucket-policy.json
Every statement here is a Deny. That is deliberate: the identity policies
grant access, and this file's only job is to make certain classes of
mistake impossible no matter what an identity policy says. An explicit
Deny in a resource policy cannot be overridden by any Allow, including one
an administrator adds later in a hurry.
Block Public Access is also enabled on this bucket. Both, because they
fail differently: BPA is an account/bucket setting somebody can toggle off
in the console in two clicks, while this travels with the bucket policy
and shows up in a diff.

Statement._comment: Master plan: TLS 1.2+ for all transit. Anything over plain HTTP is refused outright.

_comment: aws:SecureTransport is true for TLS 1.0 as well. This closes that gap
and is what actually implements 'TLS 1.2+' rather than merely 'TLS'.
The bucket has a default encryption rule, so an upload with no
encryption header is encrypted anyway and this statement never fires
in normal operation. It exists for the case where somebody explicitly
asks for something weaker: `x-amz-server-side-encryption: AES256` is
SSE-S3, which is real encryption but is NOT attributable in CloudTrail
and cannot be revoked by disabling a key. For biometric data that
distinction is the whole reason SSE-KMS was chosen.
Encrypting with a key outside this project would put the objects
beyond the reach of the key policy, the rotation schedule and the
CloudTrail trail that make them auditable.
The containment statement. Only the AI service task role and the
backend task role may touch a selfie -- not a developer's console
session, not another service's role, not a future task somebody wires
up without thinking about it.
NotPrincipal with Deny is a sharp tool and is used carefully here: the
root ARN is in the exclusion list so the account owner cannot lock
themselves out of their own bucket, which is an unrecoverable state
short of contacting AWS support.
